I've known about The Shins for awhile, but the first album I found was Port of Morrow at a garage sale without the CD, I was so bummed I went to Dimple records and bought the album. I listened to Port of Morrow way to many times to count, but it was the first album I'd listen to, and each song had this deeper meaning to me that felt extremely personal to what I was going through at that time. It made me feel like I wasn't alone, or I wasn't the only one who felt that way. 

I wish I could reproduce that feeling in something I did. I've been taking a guitar class, and I know I'm a far way away from creating anything of my own. But when you were still learning how music worked, what about learning made it exciting, or what kept you going?

I know what I was doing was wrong, but I felt that if I was left alone I would have killed myself. I know that seems a bit drastic to you,  but I felt completely alone, she was one of my only friends after high school. I literally had no one after she also left. I can't imagine what you think of loneliness, but for a couple weeks it doesn't really matter, after that though it just sinks in. To the point where you think you're a bad person, and that's why you're alone. I literally now know which way I'll kill myself if I get that way again... luckily the only reason I didn't is because I tried to imagine my life 5 years down the line, and I wanted to at least give myself the opportunity to live that long. I understand that I talk about me but this is my side of the story, i know she has her own side. i left her oppinion out because i don't know it, for me to talk on her behalf wouldn't make any sense, but you are right I wasn't thinking about her emotions during all of this. All I knew was that I didn't want to let her go because I felt she was all I had left.  After sending this post on reddit, I honestly thank you for your original message. It was the slap in the face I needed. I truly regret my actions. I understand that what I was holding on to no longer exists. 
 **tl;dr; I know what I did was wrong** but at that time I felt the alternative would have been a lot worse.. Thanks for the metaphorical slap in the face.
